newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: LatAm shares seen slow as Caracas rises on CANTV.
newsitem.headline: LatAm shares seen slow as Caracas rises on CANTV.

text.p: High interest rates in Chile, consolidating share prices in Argentina, disappointing economic data in Mexico, and heavy political weather in Brazil were seen weighing on Latin American stocks this week, traders and analysts said.

Only Venezuelan shares look set to rise. A new dawn broke for the Caracas bourse on Friday with the successful $1.1 billion global market debut of national telephone company CANTV -- one of the largest offerings to come out of Latin America in recent years.
"I see a more active market, with rising prices, deeper volume and greater investor interest," Cavelba broker Johann Gomez.
The 73 million shares placed locally are expected to send Caracas stocks for a loop, drawing greater foreign interest that should spill over into Venezuelan equities generally.
On Friday, the 19-share index closed up 3.4 percent on the week at 6,212.64, with accelerating gains seen for the rest of the year.
In Chile, September's five percent economic growth figure released Monday dashed hopes of an early cut in interest rates and of any advances on the stock exchange.

"We expect it (the bolsa) to stay depressed until the authorities signal that rates are going to come down," said Larrain Vial analyst Iva Longeri. Analysts do not expect that until well into next year.
A long drought is also expected to weigh on key hydro- electric stocks in the blue-chip IPSA index, which edged up 0.5 percent to close at 95.75 last week.
With no key data expected, Argentina's MerVal index was seen pausing for breath at around 600 points after rising on recent signs of economic recovery.

"There is no need to worry about small corrections in the market; the 600 to 610 range is merely a resting level that serves to consolidate the higher tendency," said C&E Consultants in an investors' note.
The index closed Friday at 607.06, up 0.64 percent on the week.
In Mexico, a bearish mood was seen prevailing after shares slumped for the sixth consecutive session on Friday after disappointing retail data.
"The figures showed that economic recovery has yet to reach consumers, which is worrying. We foresee no news for now that could kick-start the bourse," said one trader.
The blue chip IPC index closed the week 2.86 percent down at 3,288.29.

In Brazil, economic data is expected to pay second fiddle to politics with key votes expected Tuesday on a re-election amendment for President Fernando Henrique Cardoso and a privatization bill for mining giant Vale do Rio Doce. Both bills face strong opposition.

However, news of the restructuring of state bank Banespa, plus the possible release of third quarter GDP figures -- seen at six percent or more, may break the barrier and lend heart to the Bovespa index, which ended last week up 1.8 percent at 66,453 points.
